text:
Sophia: Heads-up — customer (Acme) just escalated a rerank failure. They hit a limit when reranking ~120 docs + a verbose query. Customer sees a 413 and an error body that says "request too large" with no token counts. They want clear guidance on what to shorten and whether we can auto-truncate.

Alex (Acme): "I sent a query + 120 docs, each ~2–3kb. Got 413 and 'request too large' — no idea if the query or docs are the problem. We tried splitting but not sure how to size things."

Sophia: Copy of the exact request they sent (sanitized):
```
POST /v1/rerank HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.ai
Authorization: Bearer ***
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "query": "Why did revenue drop this quarter? Long, detailed prompt with examples... (approx 1.2k chars)",
  "documents": [ {"id": "d1", "text": "...~2.6kb..."}, {"id": "d2", "text": "..."}, /* ~120 items */ ]
}
```

Response they received:
```json
HTTP/1.1 413 Payload Too Large
{ "error": "request too large" }
```

Sophia: No token counts in the response; customer asked for a recommended max docs/count or example of how to compute tokens. Filing here to triage + propose messaging change.

Mike: I pulled the trace from our edge logs (root request id: rq_0f9a3). We returned a generic 413 from the ingress when body_size > 4MB. Downstream rerank service actually rejects earlier if the cumulative token estimate > 65k tokens (we cap at 65k to keep KV cache/memory reasonable). But that logic lives inside rerank-service and the ingress returns the HTTP error before we include our internal reason.

Lee: Confirming — ingress only emits HTTP 413 with no body if body too large. If the request makes it to rerank-service we return 400 with code: "input_length_exceeded" but that only happens when the JSON parse + token-est compute step runs. Looks like Acme hit the 4MB body limit so they never got the nicer 400.

Sophia: So two separate limits: body payload size (4MB) and semantic token limit (65k tokens). Customer facing message needs to explain both and give actionable next steps.

Alex (Acme): For us the main pain is we can't tell which limit to hit first. Also would be great if the SDK surfaced something like: "estimated_tokens: X, docs=Y, max_docs=Z" before call.

Mike: Agree. Short-term options:
- Update ingress to include a small JSON body with guidance on 413: e.g. {"error":"payload_too_large", "hint":"payload > 4MB. Consider truncating docs or sending fewer documents in batches (max ~N docs or X tokens)." }
- Add headers like X-Redwood-Token-Estimate-Max and X-Redwood-Body-Limit so SDKs can react.
- Long-term: streamable uploads for docs or precomputed doc embeddings + ids (we can rerank on embeddings).

Lee: Implementation note — changing ingress error body is low-risk. We can return minimal JSON from the load balancer layer. Adding headers is also straightforward. But we should be careful not to leak internal token budget numbers that will confuse customers; instead return recommended guidance.

Mike: For the rerank-service 400 path (input_length_exceeded) we should change the error payload to include these fields:
- code: "input_length_exceeded"
- query_tokens: <int>
- docs_tokens: <int>
- docs_count: <int>
- max_tokens_allowed: <int>
- hint: short sentence w/ suggestion (e.g., "truncate query to <N> chars or reduce docs to M")

Example we propose to return when it reaches token cap (customer-visible):
```json
HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
{
  "error": "input_length_exceeded",
  "query_tokens": 1500,
  "docs_tokens": 67234,
  "docs_count": 120,
  "max_tokens_allowed": 65000,
  "hint": "Reduce documents or trim long doc fields. Try batching docs in groups of ~20 or use embeddings-based rerank."
}
```
Sophia: That looks good. For the ingress 413 we should similarly provide: code: "payload_too_large", body_bytes: N, body_limit_bytes: 4194304, hint: ...

Lee: I'll spin a tiny patch for the ingress to return JSON for 413s. I'll also add the header X-Redwood-Body-Limit: 4194304 and X-Redwood-Recommended-Batch-Docs: 20. Patch target: canary next Tue.

Mike: I'll update rerank-service to emit the extended input_length_exceeded payload. Also adding a log line with token breakdown so SRE can triage without forcing customers to paste giant requests. Example log:
```
INFO rerank: request_id=rq_0f9a3 query_tokens=1500 docs_tokens=67234 docs_count=120 max_tokens=65000
```

Sophia: Can we add a small snippet for customer-facing KB / support reply? Suggested reply:

"Thanks — we see your request hit our payload limit. This can happen for two reasons: 1) the raw HTTP body exceeded our 4MB ingress limit, or 2) the combined token estimate for query+documents exceeded our internal token cap (65k tokens). To fix: try batching documents into groups of ~20, shorten very long doc fields, or switch to an embeddings + id-based rerank (send embeddings instead of full doc text). We're rolling out clearer error messages so future responses will include exact token counts and recommended batch sizes. If you'd like, we can take your payload and suggest a split.

Best, Sophia (Support)"

Alex (Acme): Thanks — that would help. We'll try batching then ping if still issues. Also please let us know when the clearer errors are live.

OpsBot: Incident note created: INC-3421 — rerank payload/limit clarity. Assigned to Lee, Mike.

Sophia: Action items:
- Lee: ingress 413 JSON + headers (canary Tue) — due: 2026-03-17.
- Mike: rerank-service error payload + logs (canary Wed) — due: 2026-03-18.
- Mike & DevEx: add a short SDK warning when payload > 1MB with token estimate (follow-up RFC).
- Support: publish KB with examples (batch sizes, curl snippets) once canaries pass.

Lee: I'll attach a small repro script here for internal testing (local body generator):
```bash
python - <<PY
import json, random
q = 'why revenue drop ' * 100
docs = [{'id': f'd{i}', 'text': 'x'*2500} for i in range(120)]
print(json.dumps({'query': q, 'documents': docs})[:200])
PY
```

Mike: For QA, we'll test three cases: 1) big body >4MB -> expect 413 JSON, 2) body <4MB but token count >65k -> expect 400 input_length_exceeded with fields, 3) normal small requests unchanged.

Sophia: Thanks team. I'll reply to the customer with the KB draft and let them know we have an internal ticket. Will update here when canaries are green. :thumbsup:

Lee: Note — also flagged for potential UX: the SDK could precompute token estimates client-side (we have a Python token_count util we can expose). I'll open a short PR after ingress patch.

Mike: Linking implementation PRs in INC-3421 once created.

Sophia: Closing loop — last_message: will update last_status here once canaries done.
